title: OOP Examples
description: Small Object-Oriented Programming examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Objects hold related facts
examples.description: An object keeps related values together. A property is one named value inside the object.

examples.title: Methods perform actions
examples.description: A method is a function stored on an object. It can use this to read the object that called it.
examples.code:
const book = { title: "Moon", describe() { return this.title + " book"; } };
console.log(book.describe());

examples.title: Classes are plans
examples.description: A class is a plan for making similar objects. Each object made from it is called an instance.

examples.title: Independent instances
examples.description: Each instance has its own properties. Changing one book does not change a different book.

examples.title: Constructors set a starting state
examples.description: A constructor sets up a new object. A default value is used when the caller leaves out an argument.

examples.title: Keeping data private
examples.description: A private field starts with #. Code outside the class cannot directly read or change it.

examples.title: Getters provide a value
examples.description: A getter calculates a value when you read a property. You do not call it with parentheses.

examples.title: Inheritance adds to a class
examples.description: Inheritance lets one class extend another. The child class receives methods from its parent.

examples.title: Overriding a method
examples.description: A child can replace an inherited method with its own version. This is called overriding.

examples.title: Polymorphism uses one common action
examples.description: Polymorphism means different objects can answer the same method call. The caller uses the action without choosing each object type.

examples.title: Composition builds from parts
examples.description: Composition gives an object another object to use. A bike has a bell; a bike is not a kind of bell.

examples.title: Give each class a clear job
examples.description: A class is easier to understand when it has one clear job. A basket can add prices without also drawing the whole web page.
